description: Delete LOGIC with real consumers: the server action Contact_Save is called by another server action (Contact_Import) and by the screen action Save of the screen ContactDetail. Instead of breaking both, the verb replace repoints them to the new action Contact_Store; only then does the delete pass without force. The refusal is in tests/jobs-negative/delete-action-in-use.json.

ops._why: (0) Contact_Import is public and receives a Contact record: the Verify requires the entity to be public as well (InvalidPublic_ActionParameterNotPublic)

ops.name: Contact_Import
ops._why: (1) the SECOND consumer: an action that calls Contact_Save (the first is already the screen action Save)
(1) public = entry point from another module; it is what keeps it from being a loose action with UnusedUserAction
(2) dois consumidores reais: o no da screen action Save e o no SaveOne de Contact_Import

ops.name: Contact_Store
ops._why: (3) the replacement, with the SAME signature (which is what makes the replace safe)

ops.value: Substitui Contact_Save: mesma assinatura, gravacao com o Id devolvido

ops._why: (4) the TWO consumers now point to Contact_Store, keeping the same key
(5) it has to be at zero
(5) the two consumers are here now
(6) with no consumers, the delete passes without force: brokenConsumers=0

ops.name: Contact_Save
ops._why: (7) only the node of the screen action keeps the old name; the action no longer exists
(7) the node of the screen calls Contact_Store
